name: Atari Punk Console
subtitle: Archetype · 556 dual timer (Forrest Mims 'Stepped Tone Generator')

keyIdea.eli5: Timer 1 is a steady drummer. Timer 2 makes one long beat each time it hears the drummer, and ignores the drummer until it's done. Make its beat longer than the drummer's gap and it skips beats, so the pitch drops in steps.
keyIdea.detail: That stepping is why it sounds 8-bit.

summary: Two knobs, two RC timers. Pitch sets the trigger rate; Width sets the one-shot length. Sweeping Width gives stepped, 8-bit-ish tones.

top.label: +9 V
top.eli5: Red is the + side of the battery: the push every part drinks from.

bottom.label: 0 V (ground)
bottom.eli5: Blue is the battery's − side, and here it is also ground: the 0 V floor.

source.label: Jameco: Making Music with an Atari Punk Console

job.eli5: A bucket fills through the pitch knob until the timer dumps it, over and over: a steady stream of trigger clicks.
Each click starts a pulse of fixed length; clicks that arrive mid-pulse are ignored. This is where the stepping happens.

wire.eli5: Pulses that skip some clicks: stepped pitches.

job.eli5: A door strips the steady push so only the wiggle reaches the speaker.

wire.eli5: The stepped tone, to the speaker.

job.eli5: The pitch knob: more resistance fills the bucket slower, so fewer clicks per second.

order.eli5: Between the + rail and the timing cap.

tune.higher: Bigger pitch pot: a tighter faucet at full turn, so the bottom of the range rumbles lower.
tune.lower: Smaller: the whole range sits higher.
tune.tooFar: Very big and half the knob is clicks. 555 timing resistors much below 1k waste current and heat the chip.

job.eli5: The bucket timer 1 fills and empties.

order.eli5: From the timer's watch pins to ground.

tune.higher: Bigger timing cap: a bigger bucket, slower trigger beat, so the whole drone drops in pitch.
tune.lower: Smaller: it fills fast and the drone climbs into a squeal.
tune.tooFar: Huge and it ticks like a clock; tiny and it shrieks above hearing.

job.eli5: A bucket watcher: 'two-thirds full? dump it. one-third? let it fill.'

order.eli5: First: it sets the beat everything else follows.

use.5: Timer A's output triggers timer B at pin 8 (my reading of the classic wiring).

job.eli5: The wire that carries each click from timer 1 to timer 2.

order.eli5: From timer 1's output to timer 2's trigger pin.

job.eli5: A doorbell with a cooldown: one long ring per press, deaf until the ring ends.

use.9: Timer B's output: the sound, toward the speaker.

job.eli5: The width knob: how long each ring lasts. Longer than the click gap means skipped clicks and pitch steps.

order.eli5: Between the + rail and timer 2's cap.

tune.higher: Bigger width pot: longer pulses at full turn, so more of the knob lands in the deep stepped notes.
tune.lower: Smaller: shorter pulses, brighter and buzzier.
tune.tooFar: Very big and the one-shot swallows most triggers: long silences.

job.eli5: Timer 2's bucket, which sets ring length with the width knob.

order.eli5: From timer 2's watch pins to ground.

tune.higher: Bigger one-shot cap: each pulse lasts longer (about 1.1 × R × C), so the steps drop lower.
tune.lower: Smaller: short pulses, thin and nasal.
tune.tooFar: Big and it skips so many triggers it stutters.

calc.label: with the width pot half way (250k)

parts.label: Output cap

job.eli5: A door that passes the pulses but blocks the steady push.

order.eli5: Between the timer and the speaker.

breaks.eli5: The speaker cone sits pushed out and the battery drains faster.

parts.silentNote: The steady push makes no sound, so the model can't show it. A real speaker would sit pushed out.

tune.higher: Bigger output cap: more low end into the speaker.
tune.tooFar: Very small and the deep steps vanish.

groundNote.eli5: Ground here is the battery's − side (negative ground), the usual setup.

honestyNote.eli5: Close to the real thing in behavior, because the trick is timing, which is easy to model. The board view is an auto-generated perfboard sketch.

honesty.eli5: Modeled by counting skipped triggers, which is the real mechanism, but with ideal timing.
